about: Every procedural asset the library plans, by category, with the source each one is modelled on (reading material for maths and structure only: no code is copied). Imported from the owner's list ("Each asset has a clickable source reference next to it", 2026-11-03) by tools/procedural/import_docx.py; tools/procedural/gen_library.py writes crates/evani-procedural-lib's Cargo features and placeholder table from this file. status: todo (not built), placeholder (a simple stand-in made from its name), basic (the simplest real procedural version, batch A's "1 out of 10" pass: one idea, basic maths, noise and scatter over the shared base), done (a fuller generator or a wrapped engine module). path: cpu (a mesh made on the CPU) or gpu (an engine module that draws itself). styles: the art styles (WK01..WK24, the material library's style bar) an asset builds natively; every other style falls back to Cinematic Realism (WK24), the style every asset is built for first. A game lists categories or assets in evani.toml: [modules] procedural = ["terrain", "geometry-cube"]. docs/PROCEDURAL.md.
licence_note: licence is what the source document states; licence_known is a well-known licence the document does not state (three.js is MIT). Only MIT sources are named as inspiration for a built asset (inspired_by).
